description: The Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia, in Formal Case No. 1130 and GD-2020-02-M, by Order No. 23129, dated July 27, 2026, directed the Potomac Electric Power Company to release $516,000.00 from the MEDSIS Pilot Project Fund Subaccount to Ecogy Energy within fifteen (15) days from the date of this Order.

Order No. 23129 

I. 
INTRODUCTION 

1. 
By this Order,1 the Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia 
(“Commission”) authorizes and directs the Potomac Electric Power Company (“Pepco”) to release 
$516,000.00 from the Modernizing the Energy Delivery System for Increased Sustainability 
(“MEDSIS”) Pilot Project Fund Subaccount (“MEDSIS Fund Subaccount”) to Ecogy Energy 
(“Ecogy”) within fifteen (15) days from the date of this Order. 

II. 
BACKGROUND 

2. 
As a condition of the PHI-Exelon Merger, a MEDSIS Pilot Project Fund of $21.55 
million was created to fund grid modernization projects to benefit District ratepayers.2 In Order 
No. 20286, the Commission established the Pilot Projects Governance Board (“Board”) to 
recommend pilot projects and develop Requests for Proposals (“RFPs”), which would be 
submitted to the Commission for issuance. Responses to the RFPs would be reviewed and ranked 
by the Commission, which would then select an offeror and award a contract for the pilot project 
utilizing pilot project funds.3 

1 
This Order is issued under delegated authority pursuant to Order No. 22731. See Formal Case No. 712, In 
the Matter of the Investigation into the Public Service Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, Order 
No. 22731, ¶ 2(y), issued October 10, 2025 (“The Commission’s General Counsel, or his or her designee, is delegated 
authority to act and issue orders on the following matters: . . . y. Approval of invoices for payment by Pepco from the 
MEDSIS Pilot Project Fund Subaccount to Pilot Project contractors following approval of the invoice by the 
Commission’s contract administrator for the Project and by the Chairman of the Commission.” Any party may file a 
petition for reconsideration of the General Counsel’s decision with the Commission. 

2 
Formal Case No. 1119, In the Matter of the Joint Application of Exelon Corporation, Pepco Holdings, Inc.,

3 
Formal Case No. 1130, In the Matter of the Investigation into Modernizing the Energy Delivery System for

3. 
Following the Board’s recommendation that a Solar Aggregation and Advanced 
Inverter Pilot Project (“Solar Project”) be funded from the MEDSIS Pilot Project Fund 
Subaccount, the Commission issued RFP No. PSC-24-18 on March 12, 2024. The RFP sought 
proposals for aggregating existing and/or new solar and distributed energy resource projects 
utilizing IEEE 1547-2018 standard-compliant inverter systems and inverter settings profiles to 
automatically manage hosting capacity and communications. The Commission awarded the 
contract for the Solar Pilot Project to Ecogy in the amount of $3 million in November 2024. A 
120-day Letter Contract (Letter Contract No. PSC-24-18) was executed on February 6, 2025, and 
extended three times until December 31, 2025.4 The Letter Contract was merged into a Final 
Contract (“Contract”) between Ecogy and the Commission on January 9, 2026.5 

4. 
Under the Contract, Ecogy is obligated to provide all services necessary to 
implement the Solar Project, utilizing advanced inverters and/or controls to achieve the dual 
objectives of maximizing solar capacity and deploying a replicable, lower-cost alternative to 
cellular cabinet telemetry equipment required by the utility. The Contractor must also provide all 
design, installation, and financing, deemed necessary to implement the Project as well as manage 
the operation and maintenance of the project.6 These services are to be provided at the following 
three sites: Howard University, Ainger Place, and the Shakespeare Theatre Company’s 
warehouse.7 The Commission previously approved Ecogy’s first five invoices in the total amount 
of $1,451,500 for payment under the Letter Contract. Ecogy has now submitted its sixth invoice 
(the second pursuant to the Contract) in the amount of $516,000 for payment in accordance with 
the Phase 2.2 Milestone and Payment Schedule in the Contract.8 

III. 
DISCUSSION 

5. 
The Commission has reviewed Ecogy’s sixth invoice and its associated 
deliverables, which includes, among other things, deploying the hardware system to monitor and 
control the Distributed Energy Resources (DERs), beginning flexible operation on existing 
projects, data collection and reporting, and completing the Super Meter prototype. The 
Commission determines that both the invoice and deliverables are reasonable, appropriate, and in 
accordance with the terms of the Contract. Accordingly, the Commission directs Pepco to disburse 
$516,000.00 from the MEDSIS Fund Subaccount to Ecogy within fifteen (15) days from the date 
of this Order.
